TagDesc.Blade: Swords and knives. Classes that can equip [Blade] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Blade].
TagDesc.Katana: Katanas. Classes that can equip [Katana] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Katana].
TagDesc.Spear: Spears and polearms. Classes that can equip [Spear] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Spear].
TagDesc.Hafted: Axes, maces and hammers. Classes that can equip [Hafted] can use it.
TagDesc.Staff: Staves and wands. Classes that can equip [Staff] can use it. Its Magic Power can't be combined with a [Magic Stone].
TagDesc.Bow: Bows. Classes that can equip [Bow] can use it; an attack with this tag requires an equipped [Bow].
TagDesc.Crossbow: Crossbows. Classes that can equip [Crossbow] can use it.
TagDesc.Throwing: Thrown weapons. Classes that can equip [Throwing] can use it.
TagDesc.Whip: Whips. Classes that can equip [Whip] can use it.
TagDesc.MartialArts: Fist weapons and unarmed techniques. Classes that can equip [Martial Arts] can use it.
TagDesc.MagicStone: Catalyst stones. Its Magic Power can't be combined with a [Staff].
TagDesc.Light: Light weapons. Classes that can equip [Light] can use it (e.g. Sorcerers can use Short Swords, but not other [Blade] items).
TagDesc.LightArmor: Light armor. Classes that can equip [Light Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.MediumArmor: Medium armor. Classes that can equip [Medium Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.HeavyArmor: Heavy armor. Classes that can equip [Heavy Armor] can use it.
TagDesc.Shield: Shields. Classes that can equip [Shield] can use it.
TagDesc.Bag: Adds Inventory Slots. A Bag with [One-Handed] or [Accessory] can also be equipped in those slots.
TagDesc.Head: Worn on the head.
TagDesc.DualWield: Requires a weapon in each hand.
TagDesc.Consumable: The item is lost when used. Unlike other actions, several Consumable items may be used in the same Process or during the Briefing.
TagDesc.Preparation: Can also be used with [Timing: Briefing] before combat without consuming the Briefing action (still only once).
TagDesc.NotForSale: Can't be bought or sold in shops.
TagDesc.Untradeable: Can't be traded to other characters.
TagDesc.Rare: Rare item, usually a prize or crafted.
TagDesc.SummoningWhistle: Whistle that calls a mount or companion.
TagDesc.Training: Conditioning or training. Max 2 Training skills at CR1, 3 at CR11 and 4 at CR21 (Skill Rank doesn't count).
TagDesc.Style: Fighting style. Only one [Style] skill benefits the character at a time; change it as the Setup Process action.
TagDesc.Stance: Only one [Stance] benefits the character at a time; using another ends the previous one.
TagDesc.Harmony: Bard songs. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only one Harmony active at a time, and each target only gains one of the same type.
TagDesc.ServantSummon: Druid/Summoner servants. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only one active at a time.
TagDesc.Enchantment: Enchanter skills. Last until the end of the Scene; by default only TWO active at a time.
TagDesc.Swift: Grants extra actions. At most one [Swift] action during the Briefing and during each Process.
TagDesc.Scout: Gathers information about the next Scene when used during the Briefing (only its starting state).
TagDesc.WeaponAttack: Attack made with the equipped weapon (its tags apply to the damage).
TagDesc.MeleeAttack: Requires a melee weapon; its tags apply to the damage.
TagDesc.RangedAttack: Requires a ranged weapon; its tags apply to the damage.
TagDesc.Human: Any of the Eight Good Races.
TagDesc.Spell: A magic skill that doesn't attack (blessings, healing, wards). Silenced forbids it.
TagDesc.Song: A song, hymn or magic sound. Silenced forbids it.
TagDesc.Curse: Curse: the demons' power, which isn't magic. Silenced doesn't stop it, even with [Spell] or [Magic Attack].

costs.Name: Pay Hate and Fate costs
costs.Hint: Using a skill adds its Hate cost (with the discounts of effects) and spends its Fate. Hate is only paid in a started combat; Fate always. The card shows what was paid and has an Undo button.

limits.Name: Usage limits
limits.Hint: Counts the uses of skills with a limit (1/Scene, SR/Scenario, 1/Round…) per character. A scene ends when the combat ends or with the GM tool; a scenario only with the GM tool.

actions.Name: Timing and action economy
actions.Hint: In combat, checks that a skill is used at the right time (Major, Minor, Move and Instant in your own Main Process, Setup in the Setup Process, Cleanup in the Cleanup Process) and that the Main Process action wasn't spent yet.

hatePerCombat.Name: Hate Top and Hate Under per combat
hatePerCombat.Hint: Puts [Hate Top] and [Hate Under] on the characters of every combat, so the +2 to Dodge and Hate Damage work with several combats at once, and everyone sees on the tokens who is Hate Top.

cleanup.Name: Regen and Decay in the Cleanup Process
cleanup.Hint: In the Cleanup Process of every round, Regen heals, then Decay deals damage (through Barrier). A summary is posted in the chat.

endOfProcess.Name: Statuses that end at the end of the Main Process
endOfProcess.Hint: Staggered, Dazed, Paralyzed, Silenced and Taunted end at the end of the Main Process of whoever received them. With Afflicted, the ones it protects stay.

incapacitated.Name: Automatic Incapacitated
incapacitated.Hint: 0 HP (or 0 Max HP from Fatigue) makes a character Incapacitated, and an Incapacitated character drops to 0 HP. Incapacitated, Dead and Absent combatants skip their turn (straight to Post-Action).

endOfScene.Name: End of scene when the combat ends
endOfScene.Hint: When a started combat ends: Incapacitated Adventurers get back up with full HP, Incapacitated enemies die, and Bad and Combat Statuses end. Fatigue and Weakness stay.

revive.Name: Dead Adventurers revive at the end of the scene
revive.Hint: By the rules, a Dead Adventurer revives at the end of the scene with 1 HP and [Fatigue: Max HP − 1].

cards.Name: Attack and damage card fixes
cards.Hint: Damage is tied to the right attack, and the attack card gets a damage button. Apply doesn't work on a target that still has to dodge or that dodged, and asks before applying again. Private cards are shown to the owners of the targets.

autoDodge.Name: Automatic dodge for characters
autoDodge.Hint: Characters roll their Dodge Check as soon as the attack is declared, like the enemies, and the result is already on the card. Off, the character's owner rolls it from the card's Dodge button or the HUD.

closeReach.Name: Close reaches the next squares
closeReach.Hint: House rule: a Close attack also reaches a token touching the attacker's, sideways or diagonally, so the two tokens don't have to share a square. Every other range is the system's.

fate.Name: Fate buttons
fate.Hint: Spend 1 Fate to: +1d6 on a skill's Check, reroll the hit, the dodge or a plain check, and remove a Bad Status (Fate button on the sheet's Statuses box).

content.Name: Item and monster content
content.Hint: The trigger powers of items become skills of whoever carries them, potions and jewels heal and food removes Fatigue from whoever uses them, equipped items give their statuses at the start of the scene, and homebrew monsters get their attack damage read from their text. Only what is missing is filled; nothing edited by hand is replaced.

chatTheme.Name: Parchment chat theme
chatTheme.Hint: Skill, attack and damage cards and the rolls on parchment, with the speaker's portrait.

windowTheme.Name: Parchment system windows
windowTheme.Hint: Item and monster sheets, the effect editor, the skill and class browsers, chests and shops and the dialogs in the same look as the character sheet.

iconEffects.Name: Animated icons
iconEffects.Hint: Weapon and equipment icons get a glint from level 11 and, from level 21, an aura and particles. Off, only the magic grade frames stay. Only for you.

hud.Name: Action HUD
hud.Hint: Shows a bar above the macro hotbar for the selected token: HP, Barrier, Fate, Hate and Fatigue, the checks, the skills by Timing, the items, the statuses, the turn and the pending dodges, to roll and use everything without opening the sheet. Your own setting: each player chooses.

hudCharacter.Name: HUD with no token selected
hudCharacter.Hint: With no token selected, the HUD shows the character assigned to you (players only).

turnNotice.Name: Your turn notice
turnNotice.Hint: Tells you, with a sound, when the Main Process of one of your characters starts.

turnSelect.Name: Select the token on your turn
turnSelect.Hint: When the Main Process of one of your characters starts, its token gets selected (for the GM: the enemies and NPCs no player controls).

turnPan.Name: Pan to whoever acts
turnPan.Hint: When a Main Process starts, the view goes to the acting token.

turnUntarget.Name: Clear targets at the end of your turn
turnUntarget.Hint: When the Main Process of one of your characters ends, your targets are cleared, so the next skill doesn't go to the old target.

statusLinks.Name: Clickable statuses in the chat
statusLinks.Hint: Statuses written in the cards ([Staggered], [Decay: 10], [Weakness (Flame): 5]…) become links: a click applies the status to your targets (or the selected tokens), like skill effects, until the end of the scene. Ratings with SR are worked out; missing ones are asked.

quickEffect.Name: Create an effect from a card
quickEffect.Hint: Right click a skill or item card in the chat → Create effect on targets: an effect with the skill's name, picture and text, until the end of the Process, the Round or the Scene, to track what the skill only describes in text.

hotbar.Name: Foundry macro hotbar
hotbar.Hint: Hiding the macro hotbar puts the HUD in its place; swap shows the hotbar only while the HUD is off screen (no token selected). The 1 to 0 keys keep running the macros. Your own setting: each player chooses.
hotbar.swap: Swap: shown when the HUD is gone

tokenStyle.Name: Token bars and names in the sheet's style
tokenStyle.Hint: The HP bar, Fate and the name under the tokens in the look of the sheet: a slim bar with a gold frame (Fatigue hatched at its end, Barrier in a blue sliver above), Fate as gold diamonds and the name small and light, with a soft outline that reads on any map.

tokenBars.Name: Who sees the tokens' HP bar
tokenBars.Hint: For the HP bar. The second bar (Fate) follows each token's own setting.

tokenBarsCombat.Name: HP bar only in combat
tokenBarsCombat.Hint: Out of combat the HP bar and the class Motor leave the tokens; they show on the tokens in the combat.

statusAnimation.Name: Status animation on tokens
statusAnimation.Hint: A status put on a token turns into its place among the token's icons, and one taken away leaves turning, instead of the text with its name. Each player chooses.

conditionRules.Name: Automatic effects of the conditions
conditionRules.Hint: Dice, damage, turns and stacks of the conditions: Burning in the Cleanup Process, Poisoned at the start of the turn, Exposed without Defense, Last Stand, Mirror, Bond, Freezing that freezes, Fissured that breaks the guard and the other rules of the AS REGRAS journal (IX. CONDIÇÕES DA ETERNIA).

conditionLimits.Name: What the conditions forbid
conditionLimits.Hint: Actions, targets and movement the conditions forbid (Paralyzed, Silenced, Disarmed, Grappled, Taunted, Blinded…): warn asks whether to go on; block stops the players (the GM may still go on).

creationWizard.Name: Creation wizard
creationWizard.Hint: Opens the step by step creation wizard when you make a new character.

creationCard.Name: New character card
creationCard.Hint: A card in the chat when a character is made in the wizard, with its race, class, Magic and profession.

evolutionApproval.Name: Evolving the form with the GM
evolutionApproval.Hint: On, a player's Evolve becomes a request in the chat, and the form only gives way when the GM approves. Off, the player evolves alone on reaching the stage's CR (the rite stays in the story).

dropRoll.Name: Drops: when to roll
dropRoll.Hint: When a monster's drop table rolls by itself. Whoever felled the monster gets every item and all the gold; what doesn't fit in the inventory stays in a loot pile on its square. Whoever came after the combat started (the summoned, the Rifts' waves) leaves nothing.
dropRoll.combat: At the end of the combat
dropRoll.manual: By hand only, from the monster sheet

Notice.Body:
What's new in Eternia 0.36: the art of the Empire's bestiary

  • A portrait and a token for the Empire's 28 monsters, in anime style, with Eternia's frame: a gold ring, a crimson thread and a white background.
  • The Rifts got a hexagonal token with a sparkling purple background and an animated violet light: stars on the Small Rift, an energy field on the Great Rift and a vortex on the Mother Rift.
  • Monsters already in your world keep the old art: import them again from the Bestiary compendium to see the new one.

Since 0.35: the raiding goblins, the Hollow, the Falls, the Stray who can be saved and the Mother Rift. Since 0.34: the automatic drops, the kobolds, the beasts of the Weight, the smugglers and the named beast. Since 0.33: the Race tab. Since 0.32: the races of the world, the evolution of the form and the World of Eternia. Since 0.31: the Biography, the tokens ready to play, the automatic dodge and the creation wizard redone. Since 0.30: the starting gear and the suggested attributes; in 0.30.1, the rank-up card and the status animation. Since 0.29: the new sheet and the creation wizard; in 0.29.1, the HUD's skills in three panels. Since 0.28: twenty Magias of the high categories and eleven conditions. Since 0.27: the Sun, the Counter, the Purgatory Flames and the Theft, with five conditions. Since 0.26: the Magia review, a Trait for each one and five new conditions. Since 0.25: the Slayers (White, Shadow and Poison), the Curses and sixteen more Magias. Since 0.24: Sense Link, Angel Magic, Darkness and Bind. Since 0.23: Snow, Magic Perfume, Machine Soul and Wave. Since 0.22: 14 classes, 7 physical and 7 magic, all with Magias; the Fighter, the Centurion and the Hierophant. Since 0.21: Wood-Make, Sand, Telepathy and Teleportation. Since 0.20: the Holder Magias Magic Guns, Plants, Smoke and Magic Painting. Since 0.19: Giant, Enchantment, Magic Eyes and High Speed. Since 0.18: the Magia choice in a window of its own and the class tab without scrolling. Since 0.17: the Lost Magias. Since 0.16: the elemental Magias. Since 0.15: the Blue Mage and the Take Over Magias. Since 0.14: the White Mage. Since 0.13: the Summoner with Magias. Since 0.12: the Pictomancer. Since 0.11: the Red Mage. Since 0.10: the Black Mage and the Magias. Since 0.9: the Dragon Slayer. Since 0.8: the classes with a Motor. Since 0.7: the class system and the Samurai. Since 0.6: the Sword Art Online items. Since 0.5: one icon for each item. Since 0.4: the 10 professions. Since 0.3: the 8 races. Since 0.2: 31 automated conditions.

StatusDesc.fatigue: [Fatigue: n] takes n from the Max HP; new Fatigue adds up. At 0 Max HP the character is Incapacitated. Food, rest or the Post-Game end it.
StatusDesc.weakness: [Weakness (Tag): n]: failing a Dodge Check against an attack with that tag (or any, without a tag) deals +n direct damage. Only the highest applies to each attack.
StatusDesc.incapacitated: At 0 HP: no actions, no checks, always Post-Action. Adventurers recover at the end of the scene; enemies die.
StatusDesc.dead: Out of play for the scene. Adventurers revive at the end of the scene with 1 HP and Fatigue equal to the rest of their Max HP.
StatusDesc.staggered: −1d6 on Major and Main Process actions. Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.dazed: −1d6 on Dodge Checks; no reactions to checks against them, no Obstruction. Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.rigor: No actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, no Obstruction. Ends with a Minor or Major Action.
StatusDesc.confused: −1d6 on every check and +1 Hate at the start of each Main Process. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.decay: [Decay: n]: n damage in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.pursuit: [Pursuit: n]: failing a Dodge Check deals +n direct damage and that Pursuit ends. Several stack.
StatusDesc.afflicted: Keeps Staggered, Dazed, Confused, Weakness, Overconfident, Frightened and Charmed from ending. Ends with a Minor or Major Action.
StatusDesc.overconfident: Any natural 1 on the dice is a Fumble. Ends when the character loses HP.
StatusDesc.regen: [Regen: n]: recovers n HP in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.cancel: [Cancel (Tag): n]: reduces damage with that tag (or any, without a tag) by n. Only the highest applies.
StatusDesc.barrier: [Barrier: n]: absorbs damage before HP, spending its Rating. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.hidden: Others' actions can't target them (only areas). Ends on a Major Action, dealing or taking damage, being found or at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.swimming: −1d6 on every check. Puts out Burning.
StatusDesc.flying: Ignores scene objects with [Terrain]; only flyers can Obstruct them.
StatusDesc.identified: The GM reveals the enemy's defenses, Hate Multiplier and skills.
StatusDesc.standby: Delayed their Main Process: acts after everyone who isn't on Standby.
StatusDesc.hateTop: Highest Hate in the combat: takes the Hate Damage of enemy attacks.
StatusDesc.hateUnder: Hate below the Top: +2 on Dodge Checks.
StatusDesc.absent: Out of the scene: skips their turn.
StatusDesc.paralyzed: No Main Process action nor reaction, and −1d6 on Dodge Checks. Loses the turn: ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.asleep: No actions nor reactions, and fails Dodge Checks outright. Ends on taking damage, or when someone spends a Minor Action to wake them.
StatusDesc.rooted: Held to the ground: no actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, −1d6 on Dodge Checks. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.prone: On the ground: −1d6 on their Close attacks and on Dodge Checks against Close attacks. Standing up takes the Move Action.
StatusDesc.slowed: No Move Action, and acts after everyone who isn't Slowed. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.grappled: Held by the grappler: no actions with the [Movement] tag, the token doesn't move, attacks only the grappler. Ends with a Major Action or if the grappler is Incapacitated.
StatusDesc.petrified: Turned to stone: doesn't act nor react (loses its turn), doesn't move and fails its Dodge Checks. Takes only half the damage of attacks (after Defense and Cancel). Ends at the end of its turn, the lost one (given during its own turn, at the end of the next), or when whoever petrified it is Incapacitated.
StatusDesc.silenced: No skills with the [Magic Attack], [Spell] or [Song] tags (the Curse ones still go). Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.disarmed: No weapon attacks ([Weapon Attack], [Melee Attack], [Ranged Attack], [Sword Attack] or Range: Weapon). Taking the weapon back takes a Minor Action.
StatusDesc.blinded: −1d6 on every check but Resistance, and attacks only within 1 square. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.sealed: [Sealed (Skill)]: that skill can't be used. Without a name, it seals the last skill used. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.weakened: [Weakened: n]: −n damage on attacks. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of their own Main Process.
StatusDesc.amnesia: Forgot who it is: uses only Basic skills and items (a monster, only its skills without a Cost or a Limit). Ends at the end of its turn (given during its own turn, at the end of the next).
StatusDesc.frightened: −1d6 on every check against whoever frightened them, and can't move closer to them. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.charmed: Can't attack the charmer and −1d6 on Dodge Checks against them. Ends if the charmer deals them damage, or with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.taunted: Their hostile skills must target the taunter. Ends at the end of their Main Process.
StatusDesc.dominated: The one who dominated them commands their body: their hostile skills can't target that one nor that one's allies (the GM plays the rest). Ends at the end of their own Main Process.
StatusDesc.berserk: [Berserk: n]: +n damage on attacks, −1d6 on Dodge Checks, and only skills that attack (and movement). Ends with a Major Action or at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.pacified: Can't hurt anyone: its attacks and spells still hit and give statuses, but deal no damage at all (not even that of a failed Dodge), and its servant doesn't hurt either. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.agony: [Agony: n]: takes n direct damage whenever it recovers HP (healing, Regen, Drain) and whenever it gets rid of a Bad Status (with an action or an effect that removes statuses). The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.nightmare: [Nightmare: n]: trapped in a nightmare, doesn't act nor react (loses its turn), doesn't move and fails its Dodge Checks; damage doesn't wake it. Takes n direct damage in the Cleanup Process. Ends at the end of its turn, the lost one (given during its own turn, at the end of the next); an ally can wake it (the GM removes it). The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.burning: [Burning: n]: n [Flame] damage in the Cleanup Process. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Minor Action (putting it out) or when Swimming.
StatusDesc.poisoned: [Poisoned: n]: n direct damage at the start of each Main Process and −1d6 on Resistance. The highest Rating stays. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.freezing: [Freezing: n] (up to 3 stacks): −1 Speed and Initiative per stack. On the third the character freezes: Paralyzed, and the stacks clear. [Flame] damage removes them all. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.shocked: [Shocked: n]: n direct damage on every Major Action, and no reactions. The highest Rating stays. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.soaked: [Soaked: n]: +n damage from [Shock] and [Cold]. Can't be Burning (and loses it when Soaked); [Flame] damage only dries the Soaked. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.fuse: [Fuse: n]: in the Cleanup Process it goes off: n [Flame] damage, and the Fuse ends. New Fuses add to the Rating. Ends before with a Major Action (defusing).
StatusDesc.cursed: Recovers no HP (healing, Regen and items) and effects can't give them Barrier nor Regen. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.blackFlame: [Black Flame: n]: takes n [Flame] damage in the Cleanup Process and recovers no HP (healing, Regen and items don't work). Nothing puts it out: no action, water, [Soaked] or [Swimming]. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene, when whoever lit it is Incapacitated, or with what removes Bad Statuses.
StatusDesc.exposed: The guard is down: Physical and Magic Defense are 0 and Cancel doesn't work. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.fissured: [Fissured: n] (up to 3 stacks): −2 Physical and Magic Defense per stack. On the third the guard breaks: the stacks clear, the Barrier is gone and they are Exposed. Ends with a Major Action.
StatusDesc.marked: [Marked: n]: −1d6 on Dodge Checks; failing one deals +n direct damage and the mark ends. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.doom: [Doom: n]: the Rating drops by 1 in each Cleanup Process; at 0 the character is Incapacitated. Only what removes Bad Statuses ends it sooner.
StatusDesc.hasted: A second Minor Action in each Main Process.
StatusDesc.empowered: [Empowered: n]: +n damage on attacks. The highest Rating stays.
StatusDesc.focused: +1d6 on the next check (Dodge Checks included); ends after it.
StatusDesc.mirror: [Mirror: n]: when damaged by an attack, the attacker takes n direct damage.
StatusDesc.intangible: Takes no physical damage. Ends on a Major Action or in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.lastStand: When they would drop to 0 HP, they stay at 1 HP and the status ends.
StatusDesc.awakened: [Awakened: n]: the transformation. +1d6 on Accuracy checks and +n damage on attacks. When it ends, it leaves [Fatigue: n].
StatusDesc.servant: [Servant: n]: a summoned servant fights at their side. In the Cleanup Process, it strikes the nearest enemy within 4 Sq: n direct damage, with the servant's tag. The highest Rating stays. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.sun: [Sun: n] (up to 5): +n damage on attacks and +n Physical and Magic Defense. In a combat, it rises by 1 in each Setup Process and with each Sun spell. At 5 it is noon: [The One] for a round, once per combat; then the Sun sets by 1 each round and rises no more. In a dark scene (night), it doesn't go past 2. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.theOne: Noon: takes no damage nor statuses from attacks, and its attacks deal +CR damage. Ends in the Cleanup Process (its Rating is the rounds left).
StatusDesc.counter: [Counter (Magic or Physical)]: the next attack of that type, with a single target, that hits you does nothing to you: the attacker takes double the damage you would take, as direct damage. With no type, it works against any attack, areas too. Ends after sending back a blow, or in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.grudge: [Grudge: n]: keeps the damage. Each HP you lose to attacks adds 1 (up to CR×4). A Grudge blow lets the Rating out as extra damage and clears it. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.impetus: [Impetus: n]: +n damage on attacks and +n Physical and Magic Defense. Rises by 1 at the end of each of your turns; past your CR, you lose control and become [Berserk: CR] until the Impetus ends. Ends with a Minor Action or at the end of the scene, and leaves [Fatigue: n].
StatusDesc.combo: [Combo: n]: +n damage on attacks. Each of your attacks that hits adds 1 (some spells add more). Back to 0 when you miss an attack, take damage from an attack or end a turn without attacking. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.untouchable: Takes no magic damage (the pair of Intangible, which takes no physical damage). Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.inversion: The magic damage it would take (after Defense and Cancel) heals it instead. In turn, the healing it gets hurts, and the effects that would give it [Empowered] or [Regen] give [Weakened] or [Decay] with the same Rating. Ends in the Cleanup Process.
StatusDesc.rhythm: [Rhythm: n] (up to 3): the next damage of one of your spells (or of a [Magic Attack] or [Spell]) adds +n d6, and the Rhythm ends. New Rhythms add up. Also ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.clones: [Clones: n] (up to 6): when an attack would hit you, roll 1d6: up to n, it hits a copy (nothing reaches you, no damage nor statuses) and the Clones go down by 1. Your Close attacks deal +n damage. New Clones add up. Ends at the end of the scene.
StatusDesc.bond: Half the HP damage they would take goes to whoever made the Bond, as direct damage. Ends at the end of the scene or if that character is Incapacitated.

Card.Gain: Any hit anyone lands on the Target: +1 Breach (your Stab: +2).
Card.Spend: The Execution, only on the Target, spends them all: each Breach adds 1d6 + CR. A Target left at HP ≤ [Breaches × (CR+5)] falls (not a [Boss]).

Card.SpendLesser: The Execution, only on the Target, spends them all: each Breach adds 1d6 + CR, without the fall.

Berserker.Name: Rage
Berserker.BleedIssue: Bleed costs {n} HP: you need more HP than that.

Card.Gain: +1 Rage every time an enemy attack takes HP from you; +1 more at half your HP or less.
Card.Spend: Savage Strike spends it all: (2+Rage)d6 + Rage×CR. Breath of Blood turns Rage into HP.
Card.Cap: 3 Rage, +1 every 5 CR. With Rage, weapon attacks add +[Rage × 2] to the damage.
Card.Reset: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which you neither attacked nor lost HP, lose 1 Rage.
Card.GainLesser: +1 Rage every time an enemy attack takes HP from you.
Card.SpendLesser: Savage Strike spends it all: (2+Rage)d6 + Rage×CR.
Card.CapLesser: Half the Rage cap, at least 1. With Rage, weapon attacks add +[Rage] to the damage.
Card.ResetLesser: At the Cleanup Process of a round in which you neither attacked nor lost HP, lose 1 Rage.

Card.Gain: In the Setup Process, if the token didn't move in the round before: +1. Steady Aim (Move Action): +1.
Card.Spend: Sure Shot spends all the Aim: each point adds 1d6 + CR to the damage.

Card.Reset: Moving the token loses all the Aim.
Card.GainLesser: Steady Aim (Move Action): +1. Nothing in the Setup Process.
Card.SpendLesser: Sure Shot spends all the Aim: each point adds 1d6 + CR to the damage, without [Exposed].

Card.ResetLesser: Moving the token loses all the Aim.

Card.Gain: In the Setup Process: +1 Order. Survey the Field (Minor Action): +1.

Card.Reset: At the end of the combat. Every combat starts at 0.

Tecelao.Name: Pattern

Matador.Name: Scales

Lead.skills: Three Combat skills and one General, among the class's talents and the Magic's spells.
Lead.items: The Backpack, the Adventurer's Kit and the Sandwich are free, and your class's kit comes equipped. Swap what you like in the shop; ★ marks what the class uses.
Lead.summary: The name and the portrait, and everything chosen. On creation, the sheet gets it all at once.

Done.summary: All set. Check it and create the character.

Hint.profession: Choose a profession, or decide later.
Hint.items: Buy what you like with the {n} gold, or keep it for later.
Hint.human: Choose {n} more attribute(s) for the Human's +1.
Hint.raceChoice: {name}: choose one of the innate skills.
Hint.decree: {name}: the Magic's choice is missing, below.

race.Title: What the race gives
race.One: Attributes (+2 in total), HP and Fate, added to the class's.
race.Two: Two innate skills: one General and one Combat. Some races ask for a choice among several.
race.Three: Five stages of the form: each opens at a CR (3, 7, 12 and 16), asks for a rite and gives new skills.

class.Title: What the class gives
class.One: The base attributes, the HP and the Motor: the resource only it has, which changes every round.
class.Two: Magic slots: the magic classes choose at CR 1, 5 and 10; the physical ones at CR 1 and 10.
class.Three: A Path at CR 3, the Dedication to another class at CR 5 and the Apex at CR 10.

profession.Title: What the profession gives
profession.One: A workshop: weapons, armor, potions, food, scrolls... each profession makes its kind of item.
profession.Two: A talent of its own, for the whole party.
profession.Three: It ranks up with EXP: more attempts per scenario and items of higher level.

Race.HumanBonus: +1 to two attributes of your choice
Race.PickFirst: Choose this race to mark the attributes.
Race.StagesLead: It starts at Stage I, {name}. Each stage opens at a CR, and the form only gives way with the rite.

bestial.Name: Bestials
bestial.Tagline: Ears and tail: Feline, Lupine or Vulpine.

Magic.NoSlot: The first Magic of {name} comes at CR {rank}. There is nothing to choose here for now: go on to the profession.
Magic.Lead: {name}: the Magic slot of CR 1. Hover a Magic to read its spells; click to choose.

Profession.Note: The profession can be chosen later, in the Profession tab of the sheet.

Attr.ModTip: Modifier: the attribute ÷ 3, rounded down. It is what goes into the checks.
Attr.str: Physical Defense (×2), Initiative, Athletics and Endurance.
Attr.int: Magic Defense (×2), Initiative, Knowledge and Analysis.
Attr.Note: No attribute goes above {max} now. Accuracy uses the highest modifier, and each CR after 1 adds +1 to every attribute.
Attr.SuggestWhy: The points go where the class's base is high, up to the next modifier (every 3 points).
Attr.AtMax: At the cap of {max} at creation.

Skills.Granted: Given by the race, the class and the Magic
Skills.Note: At most {max} [Training] skills at creation. The choices of the next CRs are made in the skill browser, when the character ranks up.

Summary.Name: Name
Summary.Basics: Give the {n} basic skills (Basic Weapon Attack, Move, Switch...)
Summary.Rebuild: This character already has a race or class. Creating it again replaces the race, the class, the profession and the skills they and the choices gave; the inventory and the rest stay.

Items.KitShort: {n} gold short of the whole kit
Items.Magia: For {name}: the spells use Magic Power, and the {item} adds +{n}. Swap an accessory for it if you'll lean on the Magia.
Items.SpaceTip: Inventory space: 2, plus the equipped bag's. What is equipped takes no space.
Items.Over: The bag is over its space: {used} of {max}.
Items.RareTip: Rare: usually a reward or crafted. Check with the GM before buying it.

Kit.samurai: The Scabbard cuts with a [Katana]: the Odachi is the strongest at CR 1 (Attack 6, two hands). Medium armor, and the Bracelete adds +1 Attack Power.
Kit.guardiao: In front of the party: a one-handed sword with the Broquel, the Cota de Anéis (Phys. Def. 7) and the Elmo de Ferro. The Joia do Renascimento raises a fallen ally.
Kit.berserker: Fury wants the heaviest blow: the Machado de Batalha (Attack 9) in both hands, medium armor and the Bracelete.
Kit.monge: The Chain fights with the fists: the Soqueira Kaiser is [Martial Arts], and light armor lets you dodge. The Capa adds +1 Athletics.
Kit.assassino: Two daggers (Accuracy +2 together) to open the Breaches, light armor and poisons for the Contract's Target.
Kit.cacador: The Aim shoots with a [Bow], a [Crossbow] or [Throwing]: the Arco de Caça reaches 3 Sq, and the Brinco da Acuidade adds +1 Perception.
Kit.comandante: Who gives the Orders stays standing: a one-handed spear with the Broquel, medium armor and the Joia do Renascimento for whoever falls.
Kit.matador: Dragon strikes are [Magic Attack]s: the Anel Cinzento adds +4 Magic Power, and the Soqueira keeps the fists ready.
Kit.magonegro: Everything is a spell: the Cajado de Carvalho (Magic 5) and the Anel Cinzento (+4) give Magic Power 9. The Talisman guards against magic.
Kit.magobranco: The Staff and the Ring for the spells, and two Joias do Renascimento: who heals also raises the fallen.
Kit.magovermelho: Sword and spell in one staff: the Cajado de Carvalho has Attack 3 and Magic 5, and the Ring and the Bracelete raise both.
Kit.magoazul: The souls fight with magic: the Staff and the Ring give Magic Power 9, and medium armor holds the form up front.
Kit.invocador: Who calls the spirits stays behind: the Staff and the Ring for the spells, light armor and the Enciclopédia (+1 Knowledge).
Kit.pictomante: The Wand leaves the other hand for the Broquel, and the Anel Cinzento gives the Molds their Magic Power. The Óculos add +1 Analysis.
Kit.family: A weapon, armor and what helps the class's strikes.

Evolve.SealReady: Stage {stage} · {name} can be awakened now: click to evolve.
Evolve.SealLast: The form is at its last stage.
Evolve.Lead: {name} can shed one more layer of the {race} form and reach Stage {stage}.
Evolve.NoteAsk: The request goes to the GM, who confirms the rite in play.
Evolve.NoteNow: The form gives way now; the rite is fulfilled in play.
Evolve.GmEarly: CR {rank} hasn't come yet: only the GM can bring it forward.
Evolve.Last: The form of {name} is already at its last stage.
Evolve.LastGm: {name} is at the last stage of the form. Go back to Stage {stage}?
Evolve.Stale: The form of {name} changed: the request no longer holds.
Evolve.Regressed: The form of {name} went back to Stage {stage}.
Evolve.NoGm: No GM connected to approve the request.

Card.RequestLabel: {name} asks for Stage {stage} of the form

State.stale: The request no longer holds: the form changed.

Seen.1: The form of the Taming: lives in the Empire like anyone else.
Seen.2: Still easy to hide: a hood, gloves, an illusion.
Seen.3: The creature shows in a fight; outside it, it still hides.
Seen.4: It no longer hides: the Church calls it a Beast and has it hunted.
Seen.5: It is the creature: a monster to the whole Empire.

SeenHuman.1: Common folk: the Church blesses them, and no one looks twice.
SeenHuman.2: People say the world touched this one twice.
SeenHuman.3: The aura shows in a fight, in the color of the soul.
SeenHuman.4: The Church encourages it and watches closely.
SeenHuman.5: The Chosen belongs to the Cathedral; the Transcendent is hunted.

RaceTab.Retired: This race left the list and has no stages of the form; its innate skills still count.
RaceTab.NoStages: This race has no stages of the form.
RaceTab.ChooseHint: The race gives the attributes, the innate skills and the five stages of the form.
RaceTab.BackConfirm: Take {name}'s form back from Stage {from} to {to}? That stage's skills and +1 leave the sheet.

Drops.Floor: Nobody felled it: everything stayed on the floor.
Drops.FloorNotCharacter: {name} felled it, but carries no items: everything stayed on the floor.
Drops.PileHint: A loot pile was left on the monster's square.
Drops.Undone: Undone: the items and the gold came back, and the monster can be rolled again.
Drops.Expected: Average: {rolled} G on the 1d6 · {fixed} G fixed
Drops.ExpectedHint: The average the table gives in a roll, and what always drops.
Drops.RollHint: Roll the drops now (GM), even for a monster already rolled or one that came mid-combat.
Drops.AlreadyRolled: Already rolled: the chat card has the Undo.
Drops.NoLoot: Came after the combat started: leaves no drops (only by hand).
Drops.FromText: The table comes from the description's text.

Drops.FacesHint: The faces of the 1d6 that give this item (1-3, 6) or Fixed

Drops.GrowthNow: Grew {n}: the growth rows drop {n} times.
Drops.StolenNow: Stolen gold: {n} G, back to whoever fells it.
Drops.DropHint: Drag an item onto the sheet: it becomes a row of the table, on the faces still free.
Drops.BadRange: Use the faces of the 1d6 (1-3, 6) or Fixed.
Drops.ToPart: To {name}. Didn't fit in the inventory and stayed on the floor: {items}.
Drops.ToFull: {name} felled it, but the inventory is full: the items stayed on the floor.
Drops.ToFullGold: {name} took the gold, but the inventory is full: the items stayed on the floor.
Drops.Guide: The Enemy Creation Guide asks for
Drops.GuideBoss: {value} G on the 1d6, plus a fixed Anima-mundi {n} and [Core Material] (boss)

Bestiary.Bigger: {name} no longer fits in one square.
Bestiary.Threshold: {name} gets {statuses} until the end of the scene.
Bestiary.StoleNothing: {name} reached into {target}'s purse, but found no gold.
Bestiary.OfferLead: {monster} offers {gold} G to be let go. Whoever accepts takes the gold, and it leaves the scene with no drops.
Bestiary.OfferNoCharacter: Select your character's token (or have a character assigned) to accept.
Bestiary.TroopLost: {name} loses {lost} of the band: {n} left, and its area attacks reach up to {n} targets.
Bestiary.Retreat: {name} flees with the loot: it leaves the scene with no drops.
Bestiary.RetreatHeld: {name} tries to flee, but it is held ({status}).
Bestiary.Forgot: {name} comes back, but forgot: {skill} is [Sealed] until the end of the scene.

Engulf.Swallowed: {by} swallowed {name}: [Grappled] inside until winning the test to get out.
Engulf.Through: The blow went through {by} and hit {name}, inside (1d6: {n}).

Split.Done: {name} splits: {piece} comes out next to it with {n} HP, and {name} keeps {kept}.

Bestiary.Rising: {name} fell to {by}: at the next Setup Process it rises as {as}, unless it has HP again before then.
Bestiary.RiseSaved: {name} has HP again: it no longer rises.
Bestiary.BodyBack: {risen} falls, and the body of {name} lies on the ground again.
Bestiary.BoundFall: {name} fell, and its dead fall with it: {list}.

Rift.WriteHint: Write the Sacred Tongue over the Rift: whoever is within 1 square of it spends the Major Action and rolls 2d6 + POW against {dc}. Select your token first.
Rift.WriteFlavor: Write the Sacred Tongue (2d6 + POW) against {dc}
Rift.NoWriter: Select the token of the character who will write.
Rift.TooFar: {name} must be within 1 square of the Rift to write.
Rift.NotYourProcess: {name} only writes in their own Main Process.
Rift.NoMajor: {name} already spent the Major Action of this Main Process.
Rift.Wrote: {name} wrote a line of the Sacred Tongue ({total}).
Rift.WroteCritical: {name} wrote two lines at once ({total}, critical).
Rift.Grew: {name} was hurt while writing: the Rift grows.
Rift.ClosedBy: {name} wrote the last line: the Rift closed.
Rift.GrewFall: {name} fell while writing: the Rift grows {n}.

Named.Hint: Name it: a named beast made from this monster (GM)
Named.Title: Name a beast: {name}
Named.Lead: A named beast is the one a whole guild hunts. A new monster is made from this one, in the same folder: Level +2, attributes +1, Defenses +3, 3 Fate, the [Boss] tag, stronger attacks, its drops ×4 with an Anima-mundi and a trophy, and a Mark of the Weight.
Named.Name: Name
Named.Done: {name} got its name, made from {from}: Level {rank}.
Named.header: Named beast, made from {from}: Level {before} → {rank}, and its Window shows the new Authority. Mark of the Weight: {mark}.

skin.name: Anima Hide
skin.text: Passive. Its Anima-laden hide cancels {n} of all the damage it takes (Cancel {n}).

eyes.name: Rift Eyes
eyes.hint: +1 die on Evasion, immune to Blinded, Frightened and Confused
eyes.text: Passive. It sees through the writing of the world: +1 die on Evasion checks, and it can't be [Blinded], [Frightened] or [Confused].

fury.name: Fury of the Weight
fury.hint: Berserk and Hasted at half HP
fury.text: Passive. The first time its HP fall to half, it gets [Berserk: {n}] and [Hasted] until the end of the scene.

sparks.name: Spark Blood
sparks.text: Passive. Its blood is sparks: whoever damages it becomes [Shocked: {n}].

regen.name: Regeneration of the Weight
regen.text: Passive. In a combat it has [Regen: {n}], back each Setup Process. [Flame] damage takes the Regen away until the next Setup Process.

breath.name: Breath of the Weight
breath.text: Major action. A magic attack in an area (2 squares) against Resistance: 2d6+{n} magic damage. Once used, it comes back only when the 1d6 of a Setup Process gives 5 or more.

trophy.name: Trophy of {name}
trophy.text: What one takes from {name} to prove the hunt. Worth a good price at the guild and with collectors.

Save.Offered: {name} falters: the form gives way, and for an instant you can see who they were. Whoever is engaged with them may try to save them.
Save.Hint: Save: whoever is engaged with them spends a Major Action and rolls Negotiation against their Resistance. Select your token first.
Save.Saved: {saver} reached {name} ({total} against {vs}): they are [Pacified] until the end of the scene and leave the fight, with no drops.
Save.Failed: {saver} tried to reach {name} and couldn't ({total} against {vs}).
Save.NoSaver: Select the token of the character who will try to save them.
Save.NotEngaged: {name} must be engaged with them (on the same square).
Save.NotYet: {name} still resists: they can be reached only at 1/4 of their HP or less.
Save.NotYourProcess: {name} can try only in their own turn.
Save.NoMajor: {name} has already spent this turn's Major Action.
Save.ConnectionText: A Stray that {saver} brought back when the form had already taken them. They don't quite know who they are yet, but they know who saved them.

Latch.Latched: {name} latched on to {host}: in each Setup it drains {n} HP and heals with them, and it goes wherever its target goes. While it holds on, it doesn't attack: it only drains.
Latch.OffHint: Rip it off: the one it latched on to, or someone right there (on the same square or next to it), spends a Minor Action. Select your token first.
Latch.NotLatched: That monster isn't latched on to anyone.
Latch.NoOne: Select the token of the character who rips it off.
Latch.TooFar: {name} must be right by {host} (on the same square or next to it) to rip it off.
Latch.NotYourProcess: {name} can only rip it off on their own turn.
Latch.NoMinor: {name} already spent the Minor Action of this turn.

Gaze.Asked: {name} starts the turn {n} Sq from {monster}. Meet the gaze (roll Resistance) or look away (−1d6 on attacks until the end of the turn)? Without an answer, at the end of the turn it is met.
Gaze.MeetHint: Roll Resistance against the gaze. A failure gives [Slowed] until the end of the scene; one already [Slowed] turns to stone: [Petrified].
Gaze.AvertHint: Look away: the gaze doesn't take, but the attacks roll −1d6 until the end of the turn.
Gaze.LookedAway: {name} looks away from {monster}: until the end of the turn, attacks roll −1d6.
Gaze.Failed: {name} meets {monster}'s gaze and doesn't resist ({total} against {vs}): [{status}].
Gaze.Immune: {name} meets {monster}'s gaze and doesn't resist ({total} against {vs}), but isn't [{status}].
Gaze.NotYours: Only whoever controls that creature (or the GM) answers the gaze.

Lure.Walks: {name} hears {monster}'s call and walks {n} Sq toward the call.
Lure.Woke: {name} took damage and wakes from {monster}'s call.
Lure.SourceGone: {monster} fell: {name} is free of the call.
